newsitem.title: USA: Rain interrupts Minnesota corn, soybean harvest.
newsitem.headline: Rain interrupts Minnesota corn, soybean harvest.

text.p: Midweek rain temporarily interrupted fieldwork across the eastern half of Minnesota while the west remained dry and harvest advanced during the week ended Sunday, according to the state's Agricultural Statistics Service.
Soybean harvesting was complete on 99 percent of the acreage, compared with 95 percent last week, 88 percent a year ago and 92 percent for the five-year average.

Corn harvest was 53 percent complete, compared with 25 percent last week, 70 percent last year and the 50 percent average. Moisture content for the harvested corn averaged 22 percent, up 19 percent last year, but down from the five-year average of 23 percent.
Sunflowers were 88 percent harvested, versus 66 percent last week and the five-year average of 77 percent.
Pasture and range rated condition was rated seven percent very poor, 23 percent poor, 38 fair, 31 percent good and one percent excellent.
Topsoil moisture was rated 10 percent surplus, 74 percent adequate and 16 percent short.
